newsitem.title: KENYA: OAU says Kabila faces "great expectations".
newsitem.headline: OAU says Kabila faces "great expectations".

text.p: The Organisation of African Unity (OAU) on Sunday acknowledged the civil war triumph of Laurent Kabila and his rebels and called for a broad-based transitional authority representing Zaireans of other political shades.
"Mr Kabila and the AFDL (rebel alliance) have won the civil war and the challenge before them now is to win and consolidate the peace," said OAU Secretary-General Salim Ahmed Salim.

"I hope that when Mr Kabila forms his government of transition, it will be a broad-based one, incorporating other elements of the Congo-Zaire society," Salim said in a statement faxed to Reuters in Nairobi from the OAU's Addis Ababa offices.

Salim said the OAU looked forward to working with Kabila and his new administration as Kabila embarked on "confronting the many challenges that lie ahead, especially those relating to peace, stability and socio-economic transformation".
"The people of Congo-Zaire have great expectations. So does Africa," said Salim.

Salim said he was confident Kabila's administration would lay the ground for democracy so that at the end of the transition period, "the people of Congo-Zaire can decide through the ballot their own destiny".

On Saturday, Kabila and his rebels proclaimed victory in Zaire's seven-month civil war and purged Africa's third largest nation of one of the more obvious symbols of ousted president Mobutu Sese Seko's rule -- its name. It renamed the country the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Congo is the name Zaire had on independence from Belgium in 1960 until Mobutu changed it in 1971.
